newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT-Gold soggy after break below $340.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT-Gold soggy after break below $340.

text.p: SPOT NY CLOSE * SUPPORT * RESIST * RSI14 * MA10 * MA30
Gold looked sickly after slipping through $340 support on Wednesday, and would have difficulty recovering in the near term, dealers and analysts said.
Silver was also weak after failing at $4.80 resistance, they added.
GOLD -
Prices were depressed after news emerged on Wednesday that the Belgium Central Bank planned to sell more gold in the form of commemorative coins and the spot market broke through $340.00 support.
"There's not much chance of recovery," said independent chartist Elli Gifford.
Referring to the Comex August contract, she said light support would be seen at $340 from the current downtrend but that prices would eventually gravitate to the $338.50 low.
On the upside immediate resistance was seen at $343. "And $345 is painfully difficult to clear," she added.
Analyst Mark Schimmel of Elliott Wave International, also referring to New York's August futures, said the market was now thrusting lower out of a triangle consolidation from the February 12 low.

"Taking the longest leg in the pattern, and projecting down from the end of the structure gives us an objective well below $330.00. Then, we would expect a rally back to the breakdown point," he said.
In the spot market, some support should be seen at the April 16 low of $337.50.
At 0900 GMT spot gold was quoted at $339.60/339.90, up about 60 cents from Wednesday's New York close.
SILVER -
Silver was also tired, giving up all its previous gains on Wednesday and sinking to support at $4.70.

"With the technical indicators ticking down from their uptrend, look for a period of consolidation before renewed challenges on overhead resistance," analyst Martin Squires at broker Rudolf Wolff said.
Gifford, said the market appeared neutral in the short term, but bearish in the medium term. Support in the July Comex contract stretches to $462.50, which should hold on any near-term downside move.
At 0900 GMT spot silver was quoted at $4.70/4.72, unchanged from Wednesday's New York close.
PLATINUM -
The market was taking a tentative stab at the upside, but was finding resistance at the 30-day moving average around $412.
Referring to the Nymex July contract, Schimmel said: "Any bounce from nearby levels should find initial resistance at $411.50. Secondary resistance is at $421.50."
He advised players to stand aside for the time being.
At 0900 GMT spot platinum was quoted at $411.00/415.00, up $8.00 from Wednesday's New York close.
--Eric Onstad, London Newsroom +44 171 542-8065
